name: Honestly
preview: Sarah: Before you go, one thing: what's driving the curtailment plan — a time-of-use rate that spikes, or just keeping the total bill under a number?

messages.text: I am seeing a ship date of 11/3 on the couple of miners I am looking at. Does this mean that orders are backlogged?

No backlog — that's just the batch date. The T. P2 is drop-shipped from the manufacturer, so each unit goes out on the batch it's booked into rather than sitting in a queue.

At 166 W it's about $9 a month at 10¢/kWh. What are you paying for power?
I'm paying $0.24/kWh, but I run a small space heater in my home office. This would at least offset some of the electricity cost.
Ran the power-cost calculator · 24¢/kWh

That's a fair read — a miner is a resistive heater that happens to hash. Every one of those 166 W comes back out as heat, so while the office needs heating, it's displacing heater watts one for one.

At 24¢ the Thor P2 runs about $29 a month. And it's drawing for a full block every ten minutes, for years, while stacking sats meanwhile.

Is the B30 in the running too, or is the P2 the size you want?
I have looked at the B30. Is it powered by BM1373 asics?
Read the bsb b30 page

Yes — BM1373 chips, 30 TH/s at 360–450 W, around 50 dB, $899 with the PSU built in.

At 24¢ that's roughly $62–78 a month in power, and three times the hashrate of the P2 for the same heat you're already paying a heater to make.

Want me to price the B30 out, or stay with the P2?
what is the slowest the B30 could run? how low could we bring the output?

Honestly, I don't have a verified floor for the B30's underclock — the listing only states the 360–450 W band, and I won't guess a number you'd buy on.

I've put it to the team; they pick it up at 10am ET today and the answer comes by email.

Were you looking to run it low mainly for noise, or to cap ····bill?
cap ····bill at needed times. can the B30 curtail the individual asic's? can it turn them off/on individually?
Handed to the team · No verified underclock floor or per-ASIC control spec available for the B30; won

Same answer, and I've added it to the note: I don't have confirmed per-ASIC control on the B30, so I won't tell you it does something it may not. The team has both questions — the underclock floor and the per-chip on/off — and picks them up at 10am ET today, by email.

The T. P2 sidesteps it somewhat: 166 W flat is about $29 a month at your rate, little enough that curtailing barely matters.
do all miners sold through heliumdeploy carry the harlo labs firmware?

No. Firmware comes from whoever builds the unit — Harlo on the B30, Hammer on the Thor P2, and the Bitaxe/NerdQaxe family runs AxeOS. There's no single house firmware across the catalog.

What's behind the question — are you after one dashboard for everything, or a specific feature?
i thought harlo reflashed all of the miners it sells

I don't have that confirmed, so I won't say it either way. Harlo Labs is the maker of the B30 — what you'll see on our side is the free Harlo OS Diagnostics line that rides along with a miner, which isn't the same as reflashing another maker's unit.

I've added it to the note going to the team with your other two questions.
does the harlo labs firmware support api access to the miner?

Not something I can confirm — I don't have the B30's firmware API documented on my side, and an API is the kind of thing you'd build automation on, so a guess from me is worthless.

It's on the same note: underclock floor, per-ASIC control, reflashing, and now API access. The team picks that up at 10am ET today and replies by email.

Sounds like you want to script the curtailment yourself — is that the plan?
yes

Good — that's the detail they'll answer for. Worth knowing in the meantime: a smart plug gives you crude on/off scheduling on any of these without touching firmware, it just can't dial the wattage down.

Both units are still buyable today — B30 $899, Thor P2 $369. Want me to hold off until you have the firmware answer, or price one out now?
please submit the questions to the support time
Handed to the team · Full question set submitted at the shopper's request; all four are firmware/spec

Submitted — all four questions, with the context that you want to script curtailment at peak-rate times. The team picks it up at 10am ET today and the answer comes to your email.

What email should it go to?
(email hidden)
Handed to the team · Adding the shopper's reply-to email to the open firmware/spec question set.

Got it, Scott — the answers go to (email hidden) after 10am ET today.

Anything else I can pin down for you in the meantime?
that's it. thanks.
